data.hypothesis: Reducing the inverse-distance refinement from two Newton steps to one may lower per-interaction work while retaining enough precision for the stated tolerance. The previous two-step candidate was correct and measured at 0.00068735 s, but this variant is unmeasured and must be checked independently.

memory_lessons.applicability: The two-refinement integrated candidate passed the reported correctness checks with maximum absolute error 1.3352e-5 on the largest sizes; this does not establish correctness of the one-refinement variant.
memory_lessons.claim: The integrated warp-shuffle and refined-rsqrt program was correct and faster than the earlier measured candidates, but fewer refinements require a fresh numerical check.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Check this one-refinement kernel against the FP64 oracle on all required data, then compare its timing to the two-refinement candidate.

data.notes: Only src/nbody_kernel.cu changes. launch.json and the kernel interface are unchanged. This is an unmeasured proposal; no speedup or correctness result is claimed.
